content.overview: Section 271 states the grounds for winding up by the Tribunal, and s. 272 states who may petition.
content.glance: Section 271 states the grounds for winding up by the Tribunal, and s. 272 states who may petition.
content.study: Grounds include acting against sovereignty and integrity, fraud or unlawful purpose, default in filing financial statements or annual returns for five consecutive financial years, and the just and equitable ground. Inability to pay debts as a free-standing company-court ground was removed from the Act and is addressed through the IBC. Voluntary winding up is also under the IBC. The company-court winding up that remains is the Chapter XX Tribunal route on the surviving grounds.

caseLaw.name: Hind Overseas Pvt Ltd v Raghunath Prasad Jhunjhunwalla
caseLaw.point: Just and equitable winding up of a private company is not ordered merely because of a deadlock of confidence. The facts must justify treating the company as a quasi-partnership and show that the substratum or the mutual confidence has failed.
